Random Effects for brma Objects

Source: R/wrappers.R
ranef.brma.Rd

Extracts random effect deviations from a fitted brma object. These are posterior-sample offsets from the fixed-effect predictions, analogous to random-effect deviations returned by metafor::ranef().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'brma'
ranef(
  object,
  bias_adjusted = FALSE,
  probs = c(0.025, 0.975),
  component = "all",
  simplify = TRUE,
  expand = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

a fitted brma object

bias_adjusted

whether to adjust for publication bias. Defaults to FALSE. See blup.brma for details.

probs

quantiles of the posterior distribution to be displayed. Defaults to c(.025, .975) for 95% credible intervals.

component

random-effect component to return. Defaults to "all". For decomposed models, use a component name such as "cluster", "estimate", or a brma.mv() random-effect block name. Use "total" for the summed random-effect deviation.

simplify

whether component = "all" should return a single brma_samples object instead of a one-element list. Defaults to TRUE, matching standard 2-level brma() behavior.

expand

whether to repeat random-effect contributions for every fitted observation. Defaults to TRUE (one column per estimate; the cluster block of a multilevel model labels its columns u_cluster[<cluster>|<estimate>]), except for brma.mv() random-formula models, where it defaults to FALSE. FALSE returns one column per unique grouping-level contribution in the fitted grouping order used by metafor::ranef() (u_cluster[<cluster>] for a multilevel model). Nested groups follow their original outer-to-inner order. Indicator-coded random coefficients retain one column per observed grouping-level and coefficient combination. Set to TRUE for observation-aligned output.

...

additional arguments forwarded to predict.brma for supported options such as conditional. newdata, type, quiet, output_measure, and transform are controlled by this method.

Value

A brma_samples object for a single selected/simplified component, or a named list of brma_samples objects for decomposed component = "all" output. Use summary() on a single component (as.data.frame() of it returns its draws), or as.data.frame() on the list, to obtain the displayed summary table in long form, or as.data.frame(format = "list") to retain separate component tables.

Details

Random effects are computed as the difference between the true effects (BLUPs) and the fixed-effect predictions: $$u_i = \hat{\theta}_i - \hat{\mu}_i$$

For standard (2-level) models, returns a single brma_samples object with the estimate-level random effects.

For multilevel (3-level) models, returns a list with two brma_samples matrices:

cluster

Cluster-level random effects (\(\gamma_j \cdot \tau_{between}\)), representing between-cluster deviations from the fixed effects.

estimate

Estimate-level random effects (\(\theta_i - \mu_i - \gamma_j \cdot \tau_{between}\)), representing within-cluster deviations from the cluster means.

For brma.mv() random-formula models, decomposes the Gaussian conditional means by random-effect block. The result is invariant to whether each block was sampled or marginalized during fitting. If there is only one block and simplify = TRUE, returns a single brma_samples object. Multiple blocks are returned in one flat list under their canonical fitted block names; no additional location layer or component-name prefix is added. Unique-level output is available when a block's contribution is constant within each grouping level or observed grouping-level and indicator- coefficient combination. Other random slopes generally require expand = TRUE. When the random-effect standard deviation of a block varies across the rows of one returned cell (a grouping level, or a grouping level and indicator coefficient) through a scale formula (also for the cluster component of a clustered model with a scale formula, whether normal, GLMM, or with a weight function), the unique-level output is refused with an error of class RoBMA_ranef_expand_required (also of class RoBMA_unsupported_request); use expand = TRUE. Only the components that are returned are judged: component = "estimate" of a clustered model and a block name whose own scale does not vary are returned, whereas "all" and "total" include every block. Summed component = "total" output across multiple blocks also requires expand = TRUE because different blocks need not share grouping levels.

See also

blup.brma(), predict.brma(), pooled_effect()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
if (requireNamespace("metadat", quietly = TRUE)) {
  data(dat.lehmann2018, package = "metadat")
  fit <- brma(
    yi      = yi,
    vi      = vi,
    data    = dat.lehmann2018,
    measure = "SMD",
    seed    = 1,
    silent  = TRUE
  )

  ranef(fit)
}
} # }
